finding: Measured QoS delay: 9% lower for control, 12% lower for video.
setup: RTX 5090 · 20 MHz · 23.04 MS/s · 2 × 120 s per policy · Timing misses remain.
speaker_notes:
Sequential RTX 5090 high-load scheduler comparison. One cell, two UEs, identical CPU resources: gNB 0–7, both UEs sharing 8–19, CUDA broker 20, auxiliary 22–23. 20 MHz, 15 kHz SCS, 23.04 MS/s. Normal OS scheduling; broker pacing enabled; srsUE extra RX sleep disabled. Bulk DL 70 Mb/s, UL 2 Mb/s. Interactive video DL 12 Mb/s on/off, plus 200-byte control packets at 100 Hz in both directions. Seed 1 moving Sionna robot-ring, 10 Hz updates. Run order RR, QoS, QoS, RR; 120 seconds each plus six-second drain.
Chart metric: p99 delivered-packet one-way UDP delay in each valid second, averaged within each run, then equally across the two runs per policy. Video seconds without video packets are excluded from its delay average. Control and video both belong to the interactive UE. This is not a pooled p99 or pure scheduler decision time.

Typical delay and delivery are separate: bulk traffic is intentionally offered above measured sustainable throughput. A low delivered-packet delay is not proof of no packet loss. All interactive packet counts and full-run channel starvation/overflow/gap counters are included in the report. Timing misses remain; no strict real-time pass is claimed. Two repeats at one seed/load cannot establish a general scheduler ranking.
Earlier 40 Mb/s bulk results were rechecked: RR 8.936967 ms, QoS 8.733633 ms bulk delay; all packets delivered. CPU sets, UE and channel configurations match, and only the gNB scheduler policy differs. These earlier numbers were similar, not duplicated.
